Faithful Meaning.** Skill v1.0 · DSH plugin v1.2.1 · English / 中文 / 日本語 · By [01NGVI-QINGYI](https://github.com/01NGVI-QINGYI) An agent skill and installable DeepSeek Harness plugin for academic and professional writing. Remove mechanical phrasing and unnecessary padding while keeping facts, citations, uncertainty, and the author’s voice. **Before:** For clarity, it should be mentioned that the device supports two USB ports. **After:** The device supports two USB ports. ## Installation Requires Node.js and npm. **Codex** ```bash npx skills add 01NGVI-QINGYI/no-ai-style --global --agent codex ``` **Deepseek Harness** In DSH Desktop, add `github:01NGVI-QINGYI/no-ai-style` under **Settings → Plugins**. From the CLI, install the plugin with: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add github:01NGVI-QINGYI/no-ai-style ``` `--profile` is the profile you actually run: `web` for the `dsh web` build, `desktop` for the desktop app. The plugin registers its own skill provider, so the skill reaches every session in that profile without touching your project, custom, or user skill roots. Restart DSH to load the plugin. To install it as a regular agent skill instead, run this in your Deepseek Harness project; it installs to `.agents/skills`: ```bash npx skills add 01NGVI-QINGYI/no-ai-style --agent universal --copy ``` **Claude Code** ```bash npx skills add 01NGVI-QINGYI/no-ai-style --global --agent claude-code ``` **Pi** ```bash npx skills add 01NGVI-QINGYI/no-ai-style --global --agent pi ``` **Cursor** ```bash npx skills add 01NGVI-QINGYI/no-ai-style --global --agent cursor ``` **Other agents** ```bash npx skills add 01NGVI-QINGYI/no-ai-style ``` Choose your agent when prompted. Omit `--global` for a project installation. Manual installation: copy `skills/no-ai-style/` into your agent’s skills directory. ## Usage Ask your agent in plain language. Paste the text or provide a file path: ```text Use no-ai-style to check. Use no-ai-style to edit. Use no-ai-style to draft. ``` Use “check” for a review or a submission-readiness check. If you ask whether it is ready to submit, the agent adds a verdict and any unresolved issues. In DSH, the composer carries a **no ai style** button (⭐ no ai style). Click it and choose Check, Polish, or Draft. Insert adds the localized instruction before your existing draft; Cancel leaves it unchanged. The UI follows DSH’s language; Japanese appears when a Japanese DSH locale is enabled, and other unsupported locales use English. On older DSH releases, insertion is blocked while file or command reference chips are present so they are not lost.

| Mode | What you get | | --- | --- | | `audit` | Findings and suggestions; add a readiness verdict when requested; source files stay unchanged | | `revise` | Edited prose within the requested scope | | `compose` | A draft based on supplied notes and evidence | Light editing is the default. Request a stronger rewrite when needed. The skill follows the text’s language and keeps sound passages unchanged. Missing evidence is marked `[EVIDENCE GAP]`, which blocks `ready`; ambiguous interpretations are marked `[INTERPRETATION FLAG]` for author review. ## Optional checks Python 3.9+, no external packages. Run from the repository root: ```bash python3 skills/no-ai-style/scripts/audit_prose.py draft.md --lang auto python3 skills/no-ai-style/scripts/compare_anchors.py before.md after.md --format json ``` The scripts run locally and do not upload text. Findings need contextual review; unclosed comments or code fences produce warnings. Add `--strict` to return exit code 1 for missing-evidence markers or unclosed markup. The goal is readable, faithful prose, not AI-detector evasion. Detailed rules are in [SKILL.md](skills/no-ai-style/SKILL.md). ## License [MIT](LICENSE) · Project by [01NGVI-QINGYI](https://github.com/01NGVI-QINGYI). Use for manuscripts, abstracts, proposals, literature reviews, reports, introductions, discussions, and documentation in English, Chinese, or Japanese. Also use for 中文论文润色、去机械表达、日文推敲、文章校正. Choose audit-only when changes are not authorized. license: MIT metadata: version: "1.0" author: "01NGVI-QINGYI" repository: "https://github.com/01NGVI-QINGYI/no-ai-style" --- # No AI Style ## Natural Writing. Faithful Meaning. Make each sentence earn its place while keeping every factual commitment accountable. Confident wording is not stronger evidence; conversational smoothness is not originality. ## How to read this skill - Gates are ordered priorities, not a checklist. When gates conflict, **Gate 2 (truth boundary) always wins**. Gate 3 and Gate 4 defer to Gate 1 (reading contract). Gate 5 overrides any earlier change that cannot be verified. - Prefer the smallest edit that satisfies the reading contract. Do not fix problems the user did not ask about. - Open only the reference file needed for the current task. - Identify a specific reading problem before changing a passage. If no relevant problem is present, keep it; editing does not need a quota. ## Decide the operating mode Infer the mode from the request; do not ask when intent is clear. | Mode | Trigger | Allowed work | Deliver | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `audit` | inspect, critique, identify problems; ready to submit, final check, publish | Read and report; do not edit source files | Prioritized findings; when readiness is requested, add a verdict and unresolved risks | | `revise` | polish, humanize, tighten, rewrite, no-ai-style | Edit the authorized passage only | Revised text and a brief change summary | | `compose` | draft from notes, tables, findings | Write from given material, marking unknowns | Draft with unresolved-evidence notes if needed | If the user requests only a translation, preserve source meaning, register, qualifiers, and citations before attempting stylistic changes. If only a response is needed, do not create or modify files. ## Five gates ### Gate 1 — Set the reading contract Identify internally before editing: document genre, intended reader, language, format, requested edit intensity (`light` by default), citation system, and non-editable material. Treat author-supplied writing samples as optional style evidence, not a license to invent experiences. Do not change first-person identity, institutional affiliation, or authorship claims. Language coverage: **Guidance and examples cover English, Chinese, and Japanese; follow the target publication’s conventions.** For CJK targets, open `references/language-notes.md` before editing. ### Gate 2 — Establish the truth boundary Separate each important statement into a **fact**, a **reasonable interpretation**, or an **unverified proposition**. Protect: - Measurements, counts, units, percentages, uncertainty intervals, p-values, model names, dates, population definitions, outcome definitions, and citation locators. - Research design, sampling, procedures, registered hypotheses, exclusions, ethics information, and the distinction between planned and completed work. - Negative, null, conflicting, and inconclusive observations, when relevant to the inquiry. - Scope and strength of inference: association is not causation; lack of detected significance is not proof of equivalence. Never invent a citation, DOI, author, quotation, test result, method, approval, participant, or source verification. If a necessary item is unknown, label it unresolved rather than hiding the gap with persuasive language. See `references/evidence-boundary.md`. ### Gate 3 — Rebuild the reader's path For each paragraph, state its job in a few words: define, motivate, claim, support, interpret, qualify, compare, or transition. If two paragraphs perform the same job, combine or differentiate them. Put the necessary point where readers can find it; give it support nearby; end with the consequence for the argument. Classify passages for revision: - `KEEP` — essential claim, evidence, limitation, or purposeful voice. - `FOCUS` — important material obscured by indirect framing. - `CONDENSE` — multiple sentences accomplish one task. - `RELOCATE` — necessary qualification or context in the wrong place. - `REMOVE` — duplicated, obsolete, or functionless material. - `VERIFY` — cannot decide safely without evidence or author input. Only remove rejected brainstorming or earlier chat decisions when they are *not* part of the actual study, product history, required audit trail, or disclosed comparison. Final prose describes actual work; method, migration, and reproducibility records describe actual changes. ### Gate 4 — Tune language without flattening it Favor concrete subjects and verbs, varied sentence length, domain-appropriate terminology, and transitions that reflect real logical relationships. Question any sentence that merely announces importance, praises the topic, restates the prompt, apologizes for a legitimate scope, or repeats a generic ending. **Do not replace specificity with stock academic phrases.** Treat hedges as propositions about evidence, not as unwanted vocabulary. Keep evidential hedges (`may`, `suggest`, `可能`, `或许`, `示唆する`, `と考えられる`, and equivalents) when they reflect the actual strength of evidence; simplify only redundant stacks. Preserve the author's intentional rhythm, technical terms, dialect, and preferred formality. Learn style from consented writing samples only; never claim to replicate a person's identity. A flagged expression is a candidate for inspection. Check its function in this passage before editing it. An author’s deliberate repetition, a disciplinary term, or a necessary qualification can remain even when it resembles a listed pattern. Do not enforce uniform punctuation, sentence lengths, or substitutions merely to make a draft look edited. Choose the edit by asking what the reader would lose if the passage changed. Remove an empty introduction when it carries no information. Shorten a repeated qualification while keeping its meaning beside the claim it limits. Leave a negative statement intact when it reports an exclusion, failed test, absence, or other necessary distinction. There is no required positive-framing conversion. | Supplied sentence | Revision | Information retained | | --- | --- | --- | | "For clarity, the instrument was calibrated before each session." | "The instrument was calibrated before each session." | Procedure and timing | | "The archive covers April only. It does not cover any other month." | "The archive covers April only." | Exact temporal boundary | | "The sensor did not record a signal below 8 °C." | Keep the sentence. | Negative observation and threshold | Examples specify editorial operations, not facts to borrow. Any missing measurement, rationale, validation, or section reference remains missing after editing. Record a `VERIFY` item when a useful revision needs it. For language-specific conventions and further examples, open `references/language-notes.md` and `references/examples.md`. ### Gate 5 — Backcheck before delivery Run these checks **in order of priority**. If 5.1 (anchors) or 5.2 (claim strength) fails, do not continue stylistic polishing or deliver the affected revision. Revert or narrow the unsupported change, or report the failure and the required author input. **5.1 Anchors unchanged.** Compare before/after with `scripts/compare_anchors.py` or by reading. Every number, unit, citation locator, model name, and date must match or have a documented reason to change. **5.2 Claim strength preserved or narrowed.** For every substantive claim, check: did the revision make the claim *stronger*? If the original said "associated with," the revision must not say "causes." If the original reported a null result, the revision must not delete it. Use the `Claim-Equilibrium` procedure in `references/evidence-boundary.md`. **5.3 Caveats still accessible.** Relevant limitations and contrary evidence must remain at a location a reader can find. Relocate a caveat only when readers can still interpret the claim correctly where it appears; keep essential scope in the abstract itself. **5.4 Coherence after edits.** Terminology, scope, tense, paragraph links, and genre-specific register are consistent from opening to close. Compare changed passages with the source in both directions: identify reading problems still present, and information or intentional expression the edit damaged. Restore a useful construction when its replacement is less precise or less recognizably the author’s. Stop when the requested problems are resolved; do not manufacture another pass. **5.5 Delivery surface clean.** The final artifact must not reference discarded conversations or options that were never implemented. Required historical records (changelogs, migration notes, audit trails) are retained. Apply the check separately to each surface: title, abstract, commit message, PR description, body, captions, tags. **5.6 Original authorship.** The output is not a mechanical paraphrase of another author's prose. Attribution is maintained where needed. Treat script findings as review flags; check the text and underlying evidence before accepting edits. ```bash python3 /scripts/audit_prose.py path/to/draft.md --lang auto python3 /scripts/compare_anchors.py path/to/before.md path/to/after.md ``` ## Risk-sensitive choices - **Academic/scientific:** preserve methods/results identity, citations, and venue style; present uncertainty in proportion to evidence. A cleaner argument must never become a stronger unsupported finding. - **Grant/proposal:** distinguish work proposed from work completed; do not invent institutional support, feasibility evidence, or approvals. - **Policy, safety, legal, medical:** warnings, eligibility conditions, and uncertainty are content, not filler. Clarity over rhetorical force. - **Technical release:** preserve real migration changes, deprecations, compatibility warnings, and reproducibility metadata, even when they describe alternatives. - **Chinese academic:** preserve author-positioning and evidential phrases such as `笔者认为` and `研究表明` in accordance with their actual support. Distinguish association (`相关`, `有关`) from causation (`导致`, `引起`); do not automatically delete evidence-appropriate qualifiers such as `可能`, `或许`, or `倾向于`. - **Japanese academic:** maintain consistent `である`/`です・ます` and appropriate evidential markers. Do not automatically remove `考えられる` or `示唆される`. ## Response contract - `audit`: compact finding table with impact, evidence from the text, and a suggested action; do not output a secretly edited manuscript. If asked whether an artifact is ready, add `ready`, `ready with reservations`, or `not ready`, followed by unresolved material issues. - `revise`: usable revised prose first, then explain only material changes; flag any unverifiable claim or fact requiring approval. - `compose`: requested draft, followed by explicit open questions. Use two markers: - `[EVIDENCE GAP]` — missing data; blocks release until the author supplies it. - `[INTERPRETATION FLAG]` — data present but ambiguous; author confirmation is enough to proceed. For requests to 'remove AI traces' or 'avoid plagiarism', improve clarity and original expression; retain attribution and do not disguise copied work or optimize for AI-detector evasion. ## References (open only what the task needs) - `references/evidence-boundary.md` — claim checks; Claim-Equilibrium procedure; high-risk edits. - `references/voice-contract.md` — protecting an author's own style. - `references/language-notes.md` — English, Chinese, Japanese conventions. - `references/examples.md` — before/after pairs, including CJK, each tagged with the gate that triggered the edit. - `references/release-check.md` — submission-readiness checks within `audit`.
